19.0.s.en: (1) The portion of the tribe of Simeon

19.0.0.en: When the portion of Judah was determined, it was found to be too large for the tribe, so a part of its portion was taken for the tribe of Simeon.

19.1.0.en: The number of the cities of Simeon was thirteen, because Beersheba and Sheba are two names for one city, and Beersheba had been part of the portion of Judah and was given to his brother Simeon (ch. 15:28).

19.2.0.en: Thus the borders of the portion of Simeon are, on the east and north, the portion of Judah, on the west the Mediterranean Sea, and on the south the last border of the land of the Jews (Map 8).

19.2.1.en: The tribe of Judah gave a part of its portion to the tribe of Simeon, and this shows the love among the tribes and the submission to the leader or servant, who is Joshua. Share your livelihood with the needy so that you may be satisfied together by God's graces, and submit to the Head of the Church, Christ, who gave His life on the Cross out of love for us, so that your love increases every day toward those around you.

19.3.s.en: (2) The portion of the tribe of Zebulun

19.3.0.en: The portion included the area bounded on the east by the Lake of Tiberias, on the north by the portions of Naphtali and Asher, on the west by the portion of Asher, and on the south by the portion of Issachar. It includes the city of Nazareth and Mount Tabor (the Transfiguration), and a city named Bethlehem of Zebulun, which is different from the Bethlehem of Judah, the birthplace of Christ, and Gath-hepher (the town of Jonah the prophet). Its land was very fertile, and the main trade route called the Way of the Sea, coming from the Mediterranean to the east, passed through its land (Map 8).

19.3.1.en: If the tribes took care to possess their portion in the land of Canaan, I wish you would take care of your heavenly portion, which all the good things of the earth signify; as for the good things of your heavenly portion, they cannot be expressed, and you can know something of them through the experience of prayer and contemplation, so that your soul finds rest and rejoices.

19.4.s.en: (3) The portion of the tribe of Issachar

19.4.0.en: The portion of the tribe of Issachar is bounded on the east by the Jordan River, on the north by the portion of Zebulun, and on the west and south by the portion of the western half tribe of Manasseh. In it is the city of Nain, where Christ raised the son of the widow; and it includes the plain of Jezreel, which extends from the Jordan River to the Mediterranean Sea, and its land is distinguished by fertility (Map 8). King Ahab lived in the city of Jezreel, where he took the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, and in it is the city of Shunem, where the Shunammite woman lived in the days of Elisha the prophet (2 Kgs 4).

19.4.1.en: God has given you a portion in this life that includes various gifts and abilities, which are signified by these cities that the tribe of Issachar possessed. I wish you would use these abilities for the glory of God and be faithful in them, because you are a steward in them for their Owner, who is God, to whom you will give an account of your stewardship on the last day.

19.5.s.en: (4) The portion of the tribe of Asher

19.5.0.en: It is bounded on the east by the portion of the tribe of Naphtali, on the north by the border of the land of the Jews, on the west by the Mediterranean Sea, and on the south by the portions of Zebulun and the western half of Manasseh. Its land is fertile and has minerals such as iron and copper in the northern part. From it came Anna the prophetess (Lk 2:36) and Deborah the judge (Judg 5:17). Its portion includes the city of Cana of Galilee, where Christ turned the water into wine (Jn 2:1-12), and it also includes Mount Carmel, which lies beside the Mediterranean Sea and is mentioned often in the life of the prophets Elijah and Elisha (1 Kgs 18, 2 Kgs 2, 4). Beside it were the possessions of Nabal the Carmelite, the husband of Abigail, who lived in the days of David the prophet (1 Sam 25) (Map 8).

19.5.1.en: Thank God every day for His gifts to you, that you may feel His fatherhood and love and enjoy the delight of life in His hands, for the greatness of these lands that the tribe of Asher possessed is that they are from the hand of God.

19.6.s.en: (5) The portion of the tribe of Naphtali

19.6.0.en: It is bounded on the east by the Jordan River at its springs, on the north by the border of the land of the Jews, on the west by the portion of the tribe of Asher, and on the south by the portion of the tribe of Zebulun (Map 8). In it is the city of Capernaum, in whose synagogue Christ preached and in which He performed His miracles, and the city of Chorazin (Lk 10:13, 15). And Kedesh in Naphtali, where Barak lived (Judg 4:6). And Tobit lived in the land of Naphtali before he was taken captive to Nineveh (Tob 1).

19.6.1.en: God promised His people that He would give them the land of Canaan, and here He now divides the land for them by the hand of their leader Joshua. So be confident of God's promises to you and that He will surely fulfill them, however long the time and however adverse the circumstances that surround you.

19.7.s.en: (6) The portion of the tribe of Dan

19.7.0.en: The coast of the children of Dan went out too little for them (v. 47): the Amorites seized a part of the portion of the children of Dan.

19.7.1.en: Dan was the largest of the tribes in number after Judah, and its original portion was beside the tribe of Judah, bounded on the east by the portion of Benjamin, on the north by the portion of Ephraim, on the west by the Mediterranean Sea, and on the south by the portion of Judah (Map 8). But the Amorites drove them out of some of their portion (v. 47), so they sent to search for another suitable land to take (Judg 18:2-10), and indeed they took Laish, which is Leshem (v. 47), and what is around it, which lies in the northeast of the land of the Jews, where the sources of the Jordan River are, beside Mount Hermon, which is today Mount Sheikh. The incident of the tribe of Dan's taking possession of these regions was mentioned in (Judg 18), and these events took place a little after the death of Joshua, and this incident was probably added here by the hand of Samuel the prophet, because Joshua had died.

19.7.2.en: The tribe of Dan did not surrender to the pagan inhabitants of the land seizing part of their land, but fought and possessed another part in the north. So do not surrender to the devil's wars, but resist him by the power of God, and He will give you victory over him and will give you all your spiritual needs.

19.8.0.en: After Joshua completed the distribution of the land to the tribes, he took his portion, which is the city of Timnath-serah, lying north of the mountains of Ephraim. This shows Joshua's love and care for his people before himself, and his humility, which is a type of the humble Christ in His Incarnation and His care for the salvation of His children, whatever it cost of self-giving.

19.9.0.en: With this the division of the land ended, and each one received his portion that God had determined for him.

19.9.1.en: I wish you would put others before yourself in honor and earthly good things; then you receive spiritual blessings that cannot be expressed on earth and in heaven, and if you need material blessings, God pours them out on you generously. The cities of refuge. The chapter speaks about the six cities of refuge and their law, as previously in the Book of Numbers (ch. 35); three cities were fixed east of the Jordan and three west of it, so that the one fleeing to them from any place in the country would not travel more than thirty miles.

20.0.s.en: (1) The law of the cities of refuge

20.0.0.en: The Lord asked Joshua to appoint the cities of refuge to guarantee the right of one who killed unintentionally not to be killed, as God had made clear earlier to Moses in (Num 35:9-15, Deut 19:2-10). These cities lie among the cities of the Levites, because they live among the tribes, so it is easy for the killer to take refuge in them and be under the care of God's servants the Levites.

20.1.0.en: The way of flight to those cities was easy because of the good distribution of their locations. They would prepare the roads leading to them and put crossings over the rivers so that the fugitive would find no obstacles on the way, for he is innocent and did not intend to kill, so he escapes from the avenger of blood, that is, the relative of the killer who wants to take vengeance for him. As for the one who kills deliberately, he has no place in these cities and deserves death.

20.2.0.en: When the one who killed unintentionally reaches the city of refuge, he stands at its gate and presents his case before the elders of the city; if they are convinced of his innocence, they allow him to stay in it and do not hand him over to the relatives of the one killed, but protect him from their vengeance.

20.3.0.en: After the elders of the city judge him innocent, he dwells in the city until he stands before the elders of the congregation of the children of Israel to examine his case and confirm his innocence; then he returns to the city of refuge he had entered, and stays there until the death of the great priest, that is, the high priest, and then returns with honor to his city, and none of the relatives of the one killed unintentionally can molest him, or else he will be punished. Thus he has received the penalty for his carelessness and the unintentional killing, which is to be away from his city and family during his stay in the city of refuge.

20.3.1.en: The great priest is a type of Christ, by whose death we received salvation.

20.3.2.en: God's mercies are great, for He makes allowance for the one who killed unintentionally and gives him life and safety in the city of refuge. I wish you would make allowance for everyone who wrongs you and forgive him, so that you give him a new opportunity to live with God and with you in love.

20.4.0.en: They sanctified: that is, they set apart and dedicated.

20.4.1.en: Kedesh: it lies in the portion of the tribe of Naphtali in Galilee and is different from Kadesh-barnea.

20.4.2.en: Shechem: it lies in the middle of the land of Canaan and is present-day Nabulus, 50 km north of Jerusalem. Kirjath-arba: it is the one that Caleb the son of Jephunneh possessed and is now called Al-Khalil.

20.4.3.en: The stranger: those who are not Jews living with them.

20.4.4.en: Three cities were chosen west of the Jordan River: Kedesh in the north, Shechem in the middle and Hebron in the south; and three other cities east of the Jordan River: Bezer in the south, Ramoth in the middle and Golan in the north. Moses had appointed them (Deut 4:41-43), to be used to give the opportunity of escape to every one who killed unintentionally, whether of the Jews or of the strangers living among them (Map 9). Golan, Ramoth. Map (9) Cities of refuge

20.4.5.en: The Lord calls us to take refuge in Him from the divine wrath by repentance, opening His arms to receive us; will we refuse the invitation or welcome it?

20.4.6.en: The cities of the priests and the Levites. In this chapter are determined the cities of the priests and the Levites that were given to them by God's command, with their pastures, so that they might live in them in the midst of the people without leaving them.

20.4.7.en: We notice that the priests, that is, the descendants of Aaron, and the three families of the Levites, that is, the Kohathites, the Gershonites and the Merarites, each received a fixed share of these cities.

21.0.1.en: The Levites asked for the cities of their portion, and God gave them by lot, and so they took what suffices for their dwelling needs and the pasture of their cattle from the portion of the tribes, whether east of the Jordan or west of it.

21.0.2.en: I wish we would give to each one according to what God has given us of blessing and abundance, so that our possessions are blessed by this giving, and our love toward others is established, and we feel our oneness in Christ.

21.1.0.en: Most of the cities of the priests were concentrated in the southern region of Canaan, which would become the southern kingdom in the future, because God knows that the Temple and the service of the priests would be in this region. The priests were of the sons of the Kohathites, of the descendants of Aaron (1 Chr 6:1-3).

21.1.1.en: God's ordering of your life now may not be understood at present, but the time will come when you will know that it was the best choice at its time, for God loves you and chooses for you everything that gives you rest and brings you to the Kingdom.

21.2.s.en: (3) The rest of the portion of the Kohathites and the portion of the Gershonites and the portion of the Merarites

21.2.0.en: The total of the cities of the Levites and priests was 48 cities with their pastures, among them six cities of refuge. Thus the servants were spread out in the midst of the people without isolation so that they could lead and guide them easily, as Christ shared with us by His Incarnation and dwelling in our midst.

21.2.1.en: The Levites did not take a portion like the rest of the tribes, but God gave them cities to dwell in, because God is their portion, since they were consecrated to His service. The cities in which they lived were 48 cities, which is more than the portion of most of the other tribes, for God gives His servants spiritual blessings and suffices all their material needs. So offer your love to God and serve Him faithfully, trusting in His care, which suffices your needs and even distinguishes you from those around you, so that your thanks and your service to Him increase.

21.3.s.en: (4) The completion of the distribution of the land

21.3.0.en: God fulfilled His promise to His children by giving them the land of Canaan that He had promised them, and gave them victory over all their enemies and subdued them to them, as a type of Christ's victory on the Cross and the subjection of Satan under our feet.

21.3.1.en: Trust in the power of God that supports you and gives you victory over your enemies the demons, however great your weakness and however great the power of the demons, because God loves you and keeps you from all evil as long as you hold fast to Him.

21.3.2.en: The return to the east of the Jordan and the new altar

22.0.0.en: Joshua called the men of war of the tribe of Reuben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh to thank them for keeping their covenant with Moses (Num 32) and their obedience to him in accompanying their brothers for about seven years to possess the lands west of the Jordan.

22.1.0.en: He praised their holding fast to helping their brothers until they took possession of their portion west of the Jordan. And he allowed the warriors to return to their homes, and their number was about 40,000 fighters. We notice that the Jews sometimes lived in tents even after their settling in the land of Canaan, and they often pitched their tents and stayed in them, especially in the summer season, in addition to pitching them beside their fields to take care of them; and at first they pitched tents beside the houses of the original inhabitants because those had been destroyed and needed rebuilding or repair.

22.2.0.en: He commanded them to keep obeying God's commandments and to love Him and worship Him with all the heart, then sent them away with a blessing.

22.3.0.en: They returned laden with blessings to their land, that is, the spoils they had taken from the original inhabitants of the land after they triumphed over them with their brothers of the rest of the tribes. And they divided these spoils with their brothers who had remained to guard the homes east of the Jordan, according to the law of war, while the rest of the tribe of Manasseh took its portion west of the Jordan.

22.3.1.en: After God gives you victory over your enemies the demons, do not grow slack in your spiritual worship, but thank God and enjoy being in His hands, because His love is the goal of your life and it is what protects you from Satan.

22.4.0.en: The region of Jordan: the Jordan River curves north of the Dead Sea so that it becomes in the shape of an arc and then continues its course to the north, so the shape of this region lying east of the Jordan is nearly a circle. After the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh crossed the Jordan River and reached the east of the Jordan River, they built a great altar in this part of the curved land that resembles a peninsula. That is, they built it in their possession east of the Jordan to remember God's altar. Of course they could not build it west of the Jordan, because there the tabernacle of meeting was at Shiloh, and the altar was in it, so there was no need to build altars to remember God's altars, since it was easy for them to reach the tabernacle of meeting if they were west of the Jordan.

22.5.0.en: The news of the building of this new altar reached the rest of the tribes of the children of Israel, and they were greatly enraged and considered that the two and a half tribes living east of the Jordan had apostatized from the faith in God by building an altar east of the Jordan opposite the land of Canaan.

22.6.0.en: The tribes decided to fight the two and a half tribes, and the men of the tribes assembled at Shiloh, where God's altar was, declaring their holding fast to the worship of God in His house.

22.6.1.en: I wish you would make clear the meaning of your words and actions so that others do not understand them in the opposite way, and so you gain your peace and theirs.

22.7.s.en: (3) An accepted apology and a true witness

22.7.1.en: Father: that is, the sons of Jacob from whom the tribes came.

22.7.2.en: Thousands of Israel: the people of Israel, who are counted by thousands.

22.7.3.en: In an attempt at understanding before the war, the people sent a delegation headed by Phinehas the priest, known for his zeal (Num 25:7-13), with ten chiefs for the nine and a half tribes in the west, to negotiate with the sons of the east in Gilead.

22.8.0.en: The delegation declared its objection to the betrayal of the Lord by making a strange altar, although God had forbidden this (Lev 17:8-9) when He commanded them to offer their sacrifices on one altar, which is the one in the tabernacle of meeting.

22.9.0.en: They reminded them of what happened as a result of Balaam's counsel to Balak (Num 25:1-3), of the young men of the people being made to stumble into adultery with the Moabite women in the region of Peor, the god of the children of Ammon, a matter that they remember with sorrow to this very time because many fell dead by the plague. Thus this altar of theirs would bring harm upon the whole people.

22.10.0.en: The land of the possession of the Lord ... wherein the Lord's tabernacle dwelleth: what is meant is the land of Canaan west of the Jordan.

22.10.1.en: They offered them to move and dwell with them in the west if they considered that the land of the east was unclean because there was no altar of the Lord in it, and to cease this rebellion of building a strange altar. They also made them understand how the sin of Achan harmed the whole people and caused the death of many besides him (ch. 7), that is, they warned them that the building of this altar would bring God's wrath upon all the children of Israel.

22.11.0.en: The reply of the eastern tribes to the delegation affirmed that there was no intention of betrayal, and held fast to the declaration of their faith in God by the names by which He is known in their Hebrew language, that is, the Lord God of gods, and they repeated this for emphasis and to call the Lord to witness His knowledge of their intentions and their not betraying.

22.11.1.en: Save us not this day: they do not deserve salvation, but punishment from God, if they intend betrayal.

22.12.0.en: They said that the reason for building this great stone altar was not to offer sacrifices on it apart from the altar of the Lord, or else let God punish them. But the reason was their fear that the sons of the western tribes might think in the future that the sons of the eastern tribes are not Jews and do not know God, and might prevent them from taking part in the Jewish feasts in the house of the Lord.

22.13.0.en: And the existence of the Jordan valley, whose depth is about 3,000 to 4,000 feet, would confirm their supposition that the sons of the east are strangers, so they would prevent them from worshiping God, and consequently they would lose their fear of God and be attached to the worship of idols.

22.14.0.en: God forbid that we should: a declaration of their rejection of the evil intention of betraying God and offering sacrifices on another altar.

22.14.1.en: They declared that their purpose in building this great altar was not to use it for offering burnt offerings and sacrifices on it, but to proclaim their faith in God's altar and His worship, and that they would offer their burnt offerings and sacrifices before it, that is, on God's altar in His house at Shiloh or afterwards at Jerusalem, since its shape and likeness to the altar of burnt offering would confirm their relationship with the Lord. In this way they affirmed that there was no betrayal of God in their hearts or in their conduct, and that sacrifices would be offered only on the one altar of the Lord before the tabernacle of meeting.

22.15.0.en: The words pleased Phinehas and the delegation, and they were convinced of their faithfulness and thanked them for it.

22.16.0.en: Phinehas and the delegation returned to the lands west of the Jordan and told the people what had happened, and everyone was convinced by the words and approved them, and gave up their thought of fighting their brothers.

22.17.1.en: The sons of the east called the altar a witness because it is a witness between them and their brothers to their faith that the Lord is God.

22.17.3.en: 1- The return of the Jews to the Christian faith in the last days.

22.17.4.en: 2- The altar of the Jews after the coming of Christ and His crucifixion, which became an altar without function or meaning. It is noticed that the half tribe of Manasseh was not mentioned at the end of the speech, as a kind of brevity.

22.17.5.en: I wish you would not be hasty in judging others, and would try to reach an understanding with them or reproach them so that you may clarify the truth and overcome with love all the thoughts of the devil.

22.17.6.en: Joshua's farewell address. This chapter and the one that follows it are Joshua's last speech to the people and his handing the trust over to them and bidding them farewell after advising and guiding them.
